gui.arcanism.help.page.syntax_overview.i: This spell loops forever until it runs out of energy! Use a for loop or set a valid terminating condition to mitigate this.
Simply put, executing a spell means running a few spells in order, and those spells adjust their behavior with the parameters they receive. This page introduces the syntax basics of spell sequences.
gui.arcanism.help.page.syntax_overview.n: The ',' comma here is not required. Usually the spell compiler can tell different operands apart, but if it cannot, try adding commas/parentheses to separate spell statements.
In theory a plain loop can replace a for loop, but it is still recommended to set a maximum iteration count to avoid an infinite loop lagging the server.
gui.arcanism.help.page.syntax_overview.s: This simple spell already does something: it breaks the block at the spell's own position. But many spells can be adjusted, such as the 'Explosion' spell. It needs an explosion strength to run (otherwise how would it know how big a hole to make). We simply put the number '10' as the strength to the left of Explosion:
Sometimes we do not have such a simple need and want to combine and compute data in more complex ways, for example moving diagonally up:
This spell makes the player move up.
Other spells work the same way: for example, the 'Velocity' spell needs a target and a velocity, so we put the data to the left of the spell:
This is the most basic pattern of a spell sequence.
The simplest spell is a sequence with just one spell card:
Chaining multiple spells together enables more complex behavior:
This spell makes the spell entity fly in the direction you are looking and explode as soon as it touches the ground.
When a sequence has multiple spells, they execute from left to right.

gui.arcanism.help.page.what_is_mana.entr: This mana gives nearby objects kinetic energy when released. It is widely used in machines or spells that move objects.
This mana compresses nearby objects when released. It usually shows up in breaking, shaping and similar situations, and in spells that need a squeezing effect.
This mana emits a dazzling light when released. You will use it where light is needed. Light also raises the affinity of arcanist materials, letting machines run faster or store more mana.
This mana heats nearby objects when released. You will need it to heat something, or to cast spells that involve exothermic processes.
gui.arcanism.help.page.what_is_mana.head: Harvesting and Storage
Mana Is Everywhere
gui.arcanism.help.page.what_is_mana.intr: Mana is the foundation of Arcanism gameplay; every operation in this mod depends on it. This entry briefly introduces mana, its types, and their uses.
gui.arcanism.help.page.what_is_mana.stor: Mana can generally be collected from the physical changes matching its property. Concentrating those changes with dedicated structures (generator machines) collects mana more efficiently.
Mana must be stored in an arcanist medium. Gather arcanist materials to craft mana storage containers (such as mana cells).
Common mana storage containers: mana cell, mana buffer, etc.
gui.arcanism.help.page.what_is_mana.ubiq: Mana is stored in devices such as mana cells. Releasing mana changes the physical environment around it. Mana types are defined by the physical property they change on release, and fall into four main kinds:

tooltip.arcanism.debris_clay: Excellent mana insulation; for basic magic parts.
tooltip.arcanism.machine.read_how: Directions are relative to the machine's facing; coordinates are (front/back, up/down, left/right), positive means front/up/right
tooltip.arcanism.machine.steam_turbine.i: Converts the enthalpy of hot steam into momentum mana. Higher steam flow and pressure yield more power.
tooltip.arcanism.machine.steam_turbine.u:
Feed steam into the fluid input (1 front); condensed water exits the output (2 top).
Attach a mana connector to the link point 1 up-front,
then set overclock in the GUI to produce momentum mana.
Converts steam enthalpy into temperature mana via steam-water heat exchange. Consumes steam, produces water.

Feed steam into the fluid input (1 left); water exits the output (1 right).
Attach a mana connector to the link point 1 up-front,
then set overclock in the GUI to produce temperature mana.
tooltip.arcanism.machine.pressure_relief: Converts steam pressure into pressure mana by relieving high-pressure steam. Consumes steam only, no fluid output.

Feed steam into the fluid input (on the machine itself).
Attach a mana connector to the link point 1 up-front,
then set overclock in the GUI to produce pressure mana.

Switch: on/off;
Overclock: actual power=1M×factor(W), expected power=5M×((factor+0.5)²-0.25)(W), higher factor means lower efficiency
tooltip.arcanism.machine.water_pump.intr: Consumes radiation and momentum mana to pump water. Total flow = base flow × overclock factor.
tooltip.arcanism.machine.liquid_heater.i: Heats water into steam, consuming temperature mana or fuel. Conversion cost rises with the overclock factor.
tooltip.arcanism.machine.liquid_heater.u:
Feed water into the fluid input (1 left); steam exits the fluid output (1 right); put fuel in the item input (1 up-right).
Choose mana or fuel power.
Attach a mana connector to the link point 1 up-front.
tooltip.arcanism.machine.solar_panel.usa:
Attach a mana connector on any horizontal side to join the network.
Generates automatically by day; power drops when cloudy or at night.
Open the GUI to view live power and toggle.
tooltip.arcanism.machine.solar_panel.mod: Switch: on/off; Power depends on sunlight, panel area and efficiency
tooltip.arcanism.machine.wind_turbine.in: Converts wind energy into momentum mana. Power = 0.5 × air density × swept area × wind speed³ × power coefficient.
tooltip.arcanism.machine.wind_turbine.us:
Attach a mana connector to the link point 5 blocks above the top to join the network.
Placing it high and in open terrain yields more power.
Open the GUI to view live wind speed and power.

gui.arcanism.machine.buffer.help: This chart differs slightly from the usual network info widget. The numbers on both sides still show the storage/max cache of that mana type. The middle progress bar is split into used/available/expandable according to the mana buffer's expansion state; you can expand the mana buffer for higher energy capacity while still keeping mana distributed across the network. The number in the middle of the progress bar is the ratio of the storage portion assigned to this buffer against its original total capacity, not the overall network storage ratio. You may see values above 100% when network mana is nearly full, which means the buffer's expanded storage is already being used.
